newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina scraps special export handling fee.
newsitem.headline: Argentina scraps special export handling fee.

text.p: Argentina Tuesday scrapped a special Customs handling fee for foreign trade which will generate savings of $500 million, DGI tax service and Customs chief Carlos Silvani said.
"From now on any person or company will be able to carry out proceedings to dispatch merchandise, without being forced to use the services of Customs handlers," Silvani told a news conference.
Those handlers charged between 0.5 percent and 3.0 percent of the cost of the merchandise.

Silvani said a new decree signed by President Carlos Menem deregulating foreign trade would "facilitate the placement of our products abroad...lowering operational costs and improving the real exchange rate."
"There is a pressing need to simplify all foreign trade proceedings," he said.
